subject: Proposal: Commit tiers, capacity definitions, and SLA credit scenarios
messages:
From: Amy Lawson <amy.lawson@verdantdx.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Ortiz <rafael.ortiz@verdantdx.com>, procurement@verdantdx.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity — clarify commit tiers and SLAs

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. The execs liked the performance results but procurement wants a clearer write-up before we proceed. Two asks from my side: 1) A simple commit tier table that maps GPU-pool units to expected throughput (tokens/sec or rps) and price per month; 2) Clear contract language for what triggers SLA credits and how credits are calculated — our legal team needs precise remediation examples for inclusion in the PO.

A few specifics that matter to us:
- We run mixed workloads: short chat traces (avg 120 tokens/user) and batch vectorization jobs overnight. We need both predictable p99 latency for chat and an absolute throughput floor for batch.
- Can you confirm whether a "GPU-pool unit" in your proposal is a fixed number of vGPU hours or a more abstract capacity unit that can be mapped to different instance types?
- Finally, we anticipate an initial 12-month commit with option to scale in quarter 2 if performance is as advertised — we're asking for a discount schedule for step-ups.

If you can send draft language (we can share redlines after), that would speed up approval.

Thanks,
Amy
Amy Lawson
VP Product
Verdant Diagnostics
---
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lawson <amy.lawson@verdantdx.com>
Cc: Rafael Ortiz <rafael.ortiz@verdantdx.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — clarify commit tiers and SLAs

Thanks Amy — great summary. Attaching a compact spreadsheet that maps proposed commit tiers to a canonical "capacity unit" and to expected throughput ranges for both chat p99 and batch throughput. High-level answers inline: 

- Definition: Our GPU-pool Unit (GPUU) is an accounting abstraction representing the equivalent compute in our Dedicated cluster — it maps to an average of 1x A100-80GB hour at baseline pricing, but we present it as a flexible allocation so customers can elect instance families (A100, H100) with price/commit adjustments. The contract language will define GPUU and reference a mapping table (in the attachment) that is kept in the SOW.

- Throughput guarantees: We provide two SLAs in the commit: (1) chat latency SLA measured as p99 response time at a defined baseline request size (we'll use 120 tokens for your case), and (2) a throughput floor for background batch measured as aggregate tokens/hour across the pool. If either SLA is missed, service credits apply as a percentage of the monthly committed fee (examples in the spreadsheet).

- Step-up discounts: We can include a step-up schedule (e.g., +25% capacity at a 10% marginal discount, +50% at 18% marginal discount) for scale events inside the first 12 months. Exact thresholds can be negotiated.

I'll loop in Karthik and Neha to propose redline language for the contract definitions and an example calculation for service credits.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Verdant_Commit_Tiers_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet: commit tiers, GPUU mappings, example credit calculations)
---
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com (Karthik Iyer)
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Amy Lawson <amy.lawson@verdantdx.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, Rafael Ortiz <rafael.ortiz@verdantdx.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Draft contract language: capacity unit, throughput, and credit calculation

Amy / Tessa / Rafael —

Per Tessa's note, please find below a draft of the core redline clauses we suggest adding to the MSA + SOW. This is intentionally concise so your legal team can drop into the PO: 

1) Definition of GPU-pool Unit ("GPUU"): 
"GPU-pool Unit (GPUU) means one unit of committed compute capacity as defined in the SOW. Each GPUU is equivalent to the compute resources necessary to deliver X tokens/sec for the reference model at baseline configuration. The Provider will maintain an internal mapping of GPUU to instance families (e.g., A100-80GB equivalent) and will publish any changes 30 days prior to the next billing cycle. Customers may specify preferred instance families in the SOW; pricing will be adjusted accordingly."

2) Throughput and Latency Guarantees: 
"Provider guarantees that Dedicated capacity purchased under this Agreement will meet the following service levels when operated within agreed workload profiles: (a) Chat Latency SLA: p99 response time <= 350ms for requests with 120 tokens and <= 10 concurrent requests per GPUU; (b) Batch Throughput SLA: aggregate tokens processed per hour across the committed pool will not fall below 80% of the baseline throughput specified for the committed GPUU quantity."

3) Service Credits: 
"If Provider fails to meet an SLA in a given billing period, Customer is entitled to a service credit calculated as follows: (a) For Chat Latency SLA misses, credit = min(25% of monthly committed fee, 0.5% * number_of_minutes_below_SLA); (b) For Batch Throughput SLA misses, credit = min(20% of monthly committed fee, 0.25% * percentage_shortfall_over_billing_period). Credits are exclusive and do not stack for the same incident. Credits will be applied as a bill credit on the next invoice."

Notes: these numbers are starting points; we can convert the percentage formulas into a table showing sample outages/shortfalls and resulting credits so procurement/legal can easily reason about worst-case exposure.

I'll prepare a PDF with sample scenarios (attachment: VDX_capacity-metric-defs.pdf) and propose a final redline for the SOW.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Director, Product & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Amy Lawson <amy.lawson@verdantdx.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Rafael Ortiz <rafael.ortiz@verdantdx.com>, procurement@verdantdx.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft contract language: capacity unit, throughput, and credit calculation

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear draft. A few clarifying questions from legal/procurement: 

- The GPUU definition is helpful, but procurement wants the baseline numeric mapping included in the SOW itself (not just an internal mapping). Can you put the A100 equivalent and the tokens/sec baseline in the SOW table?
- The p99 value and the throughput floor look reasonable — procurement wants an explicit example showing how credits apply for a prolonged partial degradation scenario (e.g., 3 days at 65% batch throughput). From your formulas above, can you show the dollar credit for that scenario so our CFO can see exposure?
- For the step-up discount, is there a minimum notice period for step-ups and do step-ups take effect immediately or at the next monthly billing cycle?

Also attaching our SOW template to make insertion easier. We should be able to turn around redlines quickly once we see the example scenarios.

Best,
Amy

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lawson <amy.lawson@verdantdx.com>, Rafael Ortiz <rafael.ortiz@verdantdx.com>, procurement@verdantdx.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft contract language: capacity unit, throughput, and credit calculation

Amy — appreciate the quick feedback. Next steps to keep momentum: 

1) Karthik/Neha will publish the SOW table with explicit GPUU -> A100-equivalent mapping and include numeric tokens/sec baselines by model. (Deliverable: VDX_capacity-metric-defs.pdf)
2) We'll create a sample credit workbook that converts the formulas into dollar examples including the 3-day 65% throughput scenario you mentioned and a p99 degradation scenario. (Deliverable: Verdant_Commit_Tiers_v1.xlsx)
3) Step-up logistics: default behavior is a 14-day notice and step-ups take effect at the next billing cycle unless otherwise agreed; we can shortcut to immediate effect for upfront-prepaid top-ups — we'll add language to the SOW to capture both paths and options.

Attaching a draft SOW excerpt and the commit tiers workbook for your review. If they're good, can we schedule a short call Monday to lock discount thresholds and sign the PO? I'm available 9–11am PT.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference
